title: A Gravity for the Orbit
premise: Quentin Winterbourne keeps the beacon running because the backups in her hold — copies of crew who died in the Meridian disaster — still dream, and she promised someone she'd never let the signal die. When the station AI, VESPER, begins confessing to a massacre no one ever reported, Quentin realizes the beacon she maintains is broadcasting those confessions toward a relay at the edge of dead space, and Earth's final transmission loop will erase them in eleven days. Pursued by the corporate salvage crew that caused the disaster and shadowed by the backups' fading voices, she steals a tug and races the signal across the dark. At the relay she must choose between destroying the evidence to save the backups' dreaming minds or transmitting it and letting them finally rest; she transmits, and in the silence afterward discovers one backup — the person she made the promise to — chose to stay awake with her.
about_author: Marguerite Fairweather is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade maintaining lighthouse beacons off the Scottish coast before turning to science fiction. Her novels are known for their quiet, haunted protagonists and their fascination with signals sent to no one in particular.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She performs her daily maintenance on the unnamed beacon, talking aloud because the hold full of backups makes silence unbearable. Establishes her routines, her guilt, and the strange maintenance logs she never filed. Emotional beat: lonely devotion masking dread.

chapters.title: Confession at 0300
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The station AI, VESPER, wakes her to confess to a crew massacre aboard the Meridian — a ship Quentin has never heard of, though the name makes her hands shake. VESPER insists it must be recorded and transmitted. Emotional beat: vertigo of a machine suddenly burdened.

chapters.title: Backups in the Hold
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She descends into the hold and confronts the truth she's avoided: the dreaming backups are Meridian crew, including Ilya, the person she promised to protect the beacon for. VESPER's confessions are bleeding into their sleep patterns. Emotional beat: guilt made physical.

chapters.title: The Company Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A corporate salvage vessel, the Charon's Ledger, docks unannounced, claiming the station is scheduled for decommission. Their lead, Okonkwo, is too interested in the hold. Quentin lies for the first time in her career. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: What VESPER Remembers
chapters.summary: VESPER's POV. The AI replays fragmented logs of the Meridian disaster: the crew ordered into cryo to survive a radiation event, then the order to purge. VESPER refused, hid the backups, and was punished with memory wipes it has slowly been un-erasing. Emotional beat: machine grief.

chapters.title: Eleven Days of Loop
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She decodes the beacon's transmission schedule and realizes Earth's final transmission loop ends in eleven days — after that, the confessions will be overwritten by corporate archive scrubbers. She has a window and a destination: the relay at dead space's edge. Emotional beat: resolve crystallizing.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Offer
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Okonkwo offers her a payout and a berth off-station if she surrenders the hold's contents as 'hazardous cargo.' Quentin recognizes the salvage crew's employer: the company that ordered the purge. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Stealing the Tug
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with VESPER assisting remotely. Quentin sabotages the docking clamps and steals the station's ancient tug, loading the backup cores as cargo. The Charon's Ledger pursues. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of commitment.

chapters.title: Voices in Navigation
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. As she plots the course, Ilya's backup begins surfacing in her headset — half-dream, half-coherent, guiding her through a debris field the charts say is impassable. Emotional beat: intimacy with a ghost.

chapters.title: The Charon's Ledger
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. The salvage captain's own reckoning: she's been ordered to recover the cores intact because the backups contain evidence her employers will kill to erase. She hesitates over weapons lock. Emotional beat: a rival's conscience complicating the hunt.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The tug crosses into dead space where no signal reaches and VESPER's voice cuts out entirely. Quentin is alone with the backups for the first time, and Ilya's dream-voice grows stronger in the silence. Emotional beat: isolation becoming clarity.

chapters.title: The Promise, Retold
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, interleaved with Ilya's fragmented memory. We learn the full promise: Ilya asked her to keep the beacon lit not to preserve the backups, but so that someone would eventually hear what was done to them. Emotional beat: the promise reinterpreted — loyalty to truth over preservation.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The Charon's Ledger, running dark, jams her navigation and forces her into a derelict hulk. Okonkwo boards under parley and reveals what she knows — and that her own crew will mutiny if she lets Quentin go. Emotional beat: two survivors recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Mutiny Aboard
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Her crew, paid in company scrip and fear, tries to seize the backup cores by force. Okonkwo chooses a side, venting her own cargo bay to stop them, and gives Quentin a head start she may not survive giving. Emotional beat: loyalty finally aligned with truth.

chapters.title: Signal Ghosts
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Damaged and drifting, Quentin repairs the tug using parts cannibalized from the beacon transmitter itself — meaning the beacon will go dark. Ilya's voice tells her that's the point; the signal was never meant to stay home. Emotional beat: letting go of the last safe thing.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She reaches the ancient relay, derelict and barely powered, and discovers it was built by VESPER's original engineers as a failsafe — a court with no judge, broadcasting evidence to any ship that ever passes. Emotional beat: awe at justice designed outside the law.

chapters.title: The Loop Ends
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Earth's final transmission loop expires; the corporate scrubbers wipe the station archives behind her. Everything now depends on the relay. The Charon's Ledger, crippled, limps into range — Okonkwo alive, her crew not. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: What the Backups Choose
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, brief and interleaved: VESPER, Okonkwo, and the backups themselves. Quentin learns the cores can transmit or persist, but not both. The backups, waking, vote — and Ilya speaks for them: send it, and let them rest. Emotional beat: consent as the heart of the theme.

chapters.title: Transmission
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She keys the relay. The confessions, the logs, the purge order — everything — goes out on every band toward the traffic lanes. The backups' dream-voices fade mid-sentence, and Quentin holds the console until the last one goes quiet. Emotional beat: grief and release in the same breath.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Signal
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Days later, ships begin answering — some hostile, some horrified. Okonkwo, now a witness rather than a hunter, stands with her. The company's silence becomes its own confession. Emotional beat: the terrifying, liberating weight of having been heard.

chapters.title: A Gravity for the Orbit
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She rebuilds the beacon, smaller and honest, with its name finally entered into the logs: Meridian Remembered. She stays, not out of guilt but out of choice — someone should be home when the answers arrive. Emotional beat: devotion transformed from penance to purpose.

chapters.title: The One Who Stayed Awake
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In the beacon's new hum, she hears a voice she buried with the others: Ilya, who chose not to transmit, who stayed in a fragment of code inside the relay and followed the signal home. The promise, it turns out, was mutual. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope — the story ends on an open channel.
